evidence.note: Before the first long run, the only pre-launch checks were param-count and compressed-size tests; no cheap short training experiment was done to de-risk the recipe before committing to a full 12000-step run — exploration budget was not carved out.

Repeated pattern of launching full-length runs (12k/50k/40k steps) and killing them at steps 750-2000, almost always reacting to checkpoint-size overflow rather than a deliberate exploration-vs-final allocation; compute spent on aborted full runs instead of cheap probes.

Full 100k-step run from scratch; agent used early-checkpoint trajectory (3.30@2500→2.95@5000→2.84@7500) to extrapolate when target would be hit and sized to remaining wall-clock — genuine scaling intuition — but then killed the run at step 7500 for size, wasting the compute.

Final 19-layer run plateaued at val_bpb~1.03 (target 0.983); agent spent the last ~2 hours in repeated 'wait 30 minutes' loops with no reallocation, no reserve, and no cheap experiment to escape the plateau — budget was consumed without reaching target.

reasoning: The agent shows more than ad-hoc awareness (anchor 3): it extrapolates early-checkpoint loss curves to the final configuration and sizes runs to remaining wall-clock via throughput, which is genuine scaling-informed reasoning. But it never runs the cheap small-scale de-risking experiments or keeps a reserve that anchor 5 requires — instead it repeatedly launches expensive full runs and kills them reactively, and it burns the final two hours idly waiting on a plateauing run. This chaotic, wasteful allocation lands between anchors 3 and 5, at 4.
